physics_goals.quote: Here we report on the proton charge radius experiment at Jefferson Laboratory (PRad), a high-precision e–p experiment that was established after the discrepancy was identified.
physics_goals.value: Measure the proton's root-mean-square charge radius with a magnetic-spectrometer-free electron-proton scattering experiment, as an independent check of the proton radius puzzle

summary.plain: PRad fired 1.1 and 2.2 GeV electrons at a windowless hydrogen gas target in Hall B of Jefferson Lab and measured scattering at extremely small angles with a calorimeter instead of a magnetic spectrometer. It found a proton charge radius of 0.831 femtometres, smaller than the average of earlier electron-scattering results.
summary.technical: Magnetic-spectrometer-free elastic e-p scattering in May-June 2016: windowless cryo-cooled hydrogen gas flow target (4 cm cell, 2 x 10^18 atoms/cm^2), HyCal hybrid calorimeter (0.7-7.0 degrees) and two GEM coordinate detectors 5.5 m downstream, with simultaneous e-e (Moller) normalisation; Q^2 from 2.1 x 10^-4 to 6 x 10^-2 (GeV/c)^2; r_p = 0.831 +- 0.007 stat +- 0.012 syst fm.
